comment: Generated by runtime/http/go/filterparse (cd runtime/http/go && go test ./filterparse -run TestWriteParityVectors -update); do not edit. The Go, TypeScript and Rust HTTP runtimes each run every vector through their filter reader (D106): filterparse.Parse in Go, readFilters in TypeScript and FilterSpec::query in Rust. reads: spec is an operation's FilterBy, its fields and each one's operators, and query a raw query string, which the runtime parses as its router does, WHATWG's form-urlencoded parser: pairs split at & alone, + a space, a % that starts no escape kept as it is; the reader answers filters, each a field, an operator and its values as the query sent them (in's and notIn's split at commas and trimmed), in the spec's field order and then the operators' (eq, ne, in, notIn, gt, gte, lt, lte, contains, isNull), or refuses the request with problem, the 400's status, code, detail and details, compared as JSON values. The reader reads a request's filter keys in ascending order of their UTF-8 bytes, so a request with two faults is refused for the same one in every runtime. A value's own type is not the reader's to check: the route decodes it as an item of a query list of the field's type. queries: filters written as the bracket form's query parameters (filterparse.Query), pairs of a name and a value, unescaped, in the filters' order; an SDK that writes a typed filter sends these pairs, and reading them back under a spec that names their fields gives the filters.
